fixes.name: deployment.set-probes
fixes.description: Change the timing of a container's existing liveness, readiness or startup probes: initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, failureThreshold, and successThreshold for readiness. Give only the fields to change, with the values the evidence supports. It can't add or remove a probe, or change what the probe calls.

root_causes.name: probe_too_strict_for_startup
root_causes.description: the app works but takes longer to start than its probes allow, so they fail it before it is ready

root_causes.name: probe_timeout_too_short
root_causes.description: the app answers its probes, but slower than their timeout allows

root_causes.name: new_version_broken
root_causes.description: a recent rollout brought a version that fails, where the one before it worked

root_causes.name: application_bug
root_causes.description: its code fails, whichever revision runs

root_causes.name: other
root_causes.description: none of these: say what in the summary

guidance:
Changing a probe's timing is right when the application works and the
probe fails it only because it is slower than the probe allows: it is
killed while still starting (killed_during_startup), or its probes time
out (probe_timeouts) on answers that come a little after the probe's
timeout. The logs then show it starting or serving normally until it is
stopped, and crashed_on_its_own is false. Each revision's probe timings
are in the rollout history: compare them with how long containers ran and
with the probe failure messages.

Decide which probes to change and to what, from that evidence: liveness,
readiness or startup, and initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds,
timeoutSeconds, failureThreshold or, for readiness, successThreshold.
Give the values the evidence supports, such as a timeout above the
answers' latency, or enough delay or failures to cover the start the logs
show, and cite them. A readiness probe made more lenient keeps sending
traffic to pods that fail it for longer: change it only when the
evidence shows readiness failing a pod that serves.

Don't change a probe, and say what you found instead, when:
- the application is failing: errors or stack traces in the logs,
  crashed_on_its_own is true, or probes get error answers from a
  container that is up. A probe failing is then a symptom.
- a recent rollout (rollout_recent) brought the failures and the revision
  before it worked: whether to roll back is another kind of incident's
  call, unless the logs show the new version only starts slower.
- something the application calls is down, and its readiness probe says
  so: a more lenient probe would send traffic to pods that can't serve
  it, and hide the outage.
- probe_kills and probe_timeouts are both false: nothing shows the probes
  failing a container that works.
